name: hcsr04
description: HC-SR04 ultrasonic distance sensor. Measures 2cm-400cm using time-of-flight of 40kHz ultrasound burst. Uses machine.time_pulse_us for accurate timing.

constructor_params.name: echo_pin
constructor_params.description: Echo pin (input, high during ultrasound round-trip)

constructor_params.name: echo_timeout_us
constructor_params.description: Max wait for echo in μs (~5m at default)

methods.name: get_distance
methods.description: Trigger a measurement and return distance in cm. Returns 500 if echo timeout.

example:
from machine import Pin
from hcsr04 import HCSR04
from time import sleep_ms

sensor = HCSR04(trig_pin=Pin(14), echo_pin=Pin(12))
while True:
    print(f'{sensor.distance:.1f} cm')
    sleep_ms(500)
esp32_notes: Speed of sound approximation: 343 m/s → 29.1 μs/cm round-trip
On timeout, returns 500 cm (not error) — caller must validate range
Min detection range: 2cm. Max: 400cm (or echo_timeout_us limit).
5V device — Echo pin outputs 5V which can damage 3.3V GPIO. Use voltage divider (1kΩ+2kΩ) on Echo line.
Uses from utime import sleep_us — see pitfalls.json. (Standard MicroPython forbids u-prefix.)
hardware_notes: Trig and Echo need separate GPIO — both 5V tolerant on input (with divider)
Use 1kΩ+2kΩ voltage divider on Echo to step 5V down to ~3.3V
differences_from_standard_mp: Standard MicroPython requires manual pulse generation + time_pulse_us. HCSR04 wraps the full measurement cycle.
